one_line: Privacy-preserving AI workout coach that exposes live pose metrics and workout controls through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Runs MediaPipe Pose in-browser to track reps, angles, tempo, and form faults; an agent can create plans, monitor metrics, and propose changes while the human approves changes via gestures.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured live workout state and phase-scoped domain actions while raw camera video stays local; general UI automation could operate controls but would not comparably access the numeric coaching loop reliably.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT claims getLiveMetrics, getSetHistory, plan and set-control tools exposed through document.modelContext.
Frame sheets show agent-created plan, tool-driven set start, changing rep metrics, and a proposed adjustment awaiting approval.
Frame sheet states the camera never leaves the tab and the AI receives numbers rather than video.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent plan-to-workout-to-metrics-to-adjustment flow with polished consistent UI, though evidence is storyboard imagery rather than an observed live run.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show plan creation, countdown, rep progression, live metrics/history, and approval modal.
Devpost screenshot shows workout controls, rep count, and an activity/tool log.
FACTS report a live demo link and seven gallery images, but no submitted video.
impact_rationale: Home exercisers have a concrete safety and coaching need; local processing and human approval directly address privacy and form concerns.
impact_evidence: PITCH identifies home-workout form and camera-privacy concerns.
Frames visibly show pose tracking, rep counting, and a proposed form-aware program change.
creativity_rationale: Combining numerical-only camera coaching with gesture-based approval while hands are occupied is a fresh, well-pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Concept explicitly separates on-device vision from agent-visible metrics.
ABOUT describes raise-hands/cross-arms approval and open-palm rest skipping.
usability_note: The visible flow is legible and hands-free gestures suit exercise, though gesture reliability and accessibility alternatives are not evidenced.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; execution is claimed from frames and packaging.
Fitness/form accuracy and gesture robustness are not independently demonstrated.
standouts: Strong privacy boundary: agent receives metrics, not camera frames.
Human-in-the-loop approval is integrated into the workout context.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-specific shared-state coaching concept with coherent end-to-end storyboard evidence and credible user value.

one_line: Shared wildfire-readiness map where humans add local knowledge and agents run bounded scenarios and stage plans.
what_it_does: Provides a deterministic La Palma incident exercise board with public terrain/history separated from synthetic scenario data; WebMCP tools inspect the board, simulate spread, compare responses, add annotations, and stage a human-reviewable plan.
leverage_rationale: The product’s core value is shared live spatial state and domain-intent agent collaboration: human annotations affect later analysis and the agent stages a plan without gaining final approval. Generic UI driving would lose precision, provenance, and state lineage.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes Zustand as shared source of truth for React controls and WebMCP callbacks.
Six domain tools include read board, inspect zone, simulate spread, compare responses, add local annotation, and stage plan.
ABOUT states every agent action changes the same interface, human annotations affect later scores, and stale proposals are rejected.
execution_rationale: The packet presents unusually complete product architecture and a coherent safety-constrained workflow, with polished map UI and explicit provenance; no live submitted video limits observed execution certainty.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show rehearsal framing, local knowledge/map evidence/AI chat concepts, and a detailed operational map with response comparisons.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows map, simulation control, response options, and ranking rationale.
ABOUT claims deterministic browser-only execution, tests for registration/state mutations/stale rejection/human approval, and no backend/API key.
impact_rationale: Wildfire planners, communities, and exercise directors have a concrete high-consequence need for rehearsable, evidence-grounded decisions; the shared map and human authority fit that need directly.
impact_evidence: PITCH identifies wildfire readiness and collaborative planning.
ABOUT grounds the board in La Palma terrain and historical burn data while clearly labeling active scenario data synthetic.
Visible demo presents bounded what-ifs and alternative response strategies.
creativity_rationale: The integrated rehearsal model—local knowledge feeding agent analysis on one persistent map with provenance and human-only approval—is an ambitious and memorable use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Frame storyboard emphasizes rehearse-first and avoiding context loss across local knowledge, map evidence, and AI chat.
ABOUT combines reversible response drafts, monotonic state lineage, synthetic/public provenance separation, and cinematic map motion.
usability_note: The map-centered workflow and explicit source labels support comprehension, but high-consequence scenario UI would need observed testing and accessibility evidence.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; agent invocation is described but not directly visible in the supplied frame sheets.
Active incident and forecast-like cues are synthetic, so the product is an exercise tool rather than operational prediction.
standouts: Human approval is deliberately kept out of the agent tool surface.
advance_reason: A high-leverage, safety-conscious collaboration model with strong visual and architectural evidence and credible impact for wildfire preparedness.
